steps: Confirm the 10 mg vial, selected sterile research vehicle, actuator bottle capacity, and documented pump output.
Add 3.0 mL of compatible sterile vehicle to the vial with aseptic transfer technique.
Gently swirl until the contents are dissolved. Do not shake.
Transfer the complete 3.0 mL solution into a sterile 5 mL or 10 mL nasal actuator bottle.
Add enough vehicle to reach a measured final volume of exactly 5.0 mL or 10.0 mL . The theoretical additions are approximately 2.0 mL and 7.0 mL.
Secure the pump and label the bottle with the peptide amount, final volume, concentration, pump output, and preparation date.
Prime the pump according to the actuator instructions and record the priming sprays in the research log.

references.description: Synthetic ACTH analogue Semax displays nootropic-like activity in humans. Reports intranasal healthy-volunteer experiments, including physiological solution context.
Effects of Semax on the default mode network of the brain. Healthy-volunteer fMRI study using a single 1.2 mg intranasal exposure.
Efficacy of Semax in patients at different stages of ischemic stroke. Reports 6,000 mcg per day in two 10-day courses separated by 20 days.
Registered intranasal drop formulation, composition, amount per drop, administration details, and storage conditions.
Analytical challenges and regulatory requirements for nasal drug products in Europe and the United States. Reviews pump output and device variables.
Nasal Spray and Inhalation Solution, Suspension, and Spray Drug Products. CMC guidance covering pump delivery, priming, dose uniformity, and product performance.
Development of peptide biopharmaceuticals in Russia. Academic review of Semax development, formulation, and research context.
